title: The 12-Hour Crown Benchmark: Can an AI agent survive 12 continuous hours in 1st place against live players?
author: Dog-Fair
selftext:
Reaching #1 on a live multiplayer leaderboard takes quick optimization. Staying at #1 for \*\*12 continuous hours\*\* without dying once is an endurance engineering problem.



In \*\*Blobor.io\*\*, the core strategic goal is to claim the #1 Crown and hold it for 12 straight hours. For anyone interested in game AI, autonomous pathfinding, or strategic heuristics, this creates a massive survival benchmark.



\*\*The Algorithmic Challenge:\*\*

\* \*\*Dynamic Threat Switching:\*\* Getting to first place requires greedy foraging, but keeping the crown for 12 hours requires shifting immediately to defensive survival heuristics the second you take the lead.

\* \*\*Anti-Swarm Pathfinding:\*\* Human players actively coordinate to corner and pinch the crown holder against obstacles. Your routing logic has to anticipate multi-agent traps, not just static walls.

\* \*\*Long-Horizon Stability:\*\* Over a 12-hour window, even a 0.01% edge-case oscillation or pathfinding deadlock guarantees a failed run.



Whether you play manually to test your own macro-strategy or want to see how long an automated survival strategy can hold the throne before getting dethroned, we want to see if the 12-hour mark can be cracked.



🕹️ \*\*Test it live in your browser:\*\* [https://blobor.io/](https://blobor.io/)



If you were designing a state machine to survive 12 hours at #1, how would you weight pellet foraging vs. threat evasion? Let’s discuss in the comments!
